IntroducedBillHeader.Sponsors: Representatives Linville, Skinner, Fromhold, Grant, Haler, Dunshee, Dunn, Santos, Armstrong, Wallace, Morris, Holmquist, Pettigrew, Schindler, Kenney, Morrell, Eickmeyer and Rodne

Bill.BriefDescription: Directing the state investment board to invest in start-up and expanding businesses within the state of Washington.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to the Washington growing business fund; adding newsections to chapter 43.33A RCW; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Washington state has many world classcompanies within its borders producing family wage jobs and benefits.The state continues to be home to entrepreneurs and innovativetechnologies, however, the future development of many of the state'semerging businesses depends on access to capital. The legislature finds that prudent targeted private equityinvestment by the state investment board would strengthen the localventure capital infrastructure, increase access to capital for localcompanies, support emerging businesses, create jobs for Washingtoncitizens, and maximize the investment returns of pension funds.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 43.33A RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The state investment board shall establish a fund of no lessthan five hundred million dollars of the board's investment portfolioin the Washington growing business fund, an account that shall be p. 1 HB 1594maintained separately and apart from other money invested by the board.Investments from the account may be made in startup and expandingbusinesses based in Washington with a substantial employment baselocated in the state. These investments may be made directly by theboard or through the board's investment advisors, including venturecapital firms. The earnings on the Washington growing business fundmust be accounted for separately from other investments by the board. (2) The purpose of the Washington growing business fund is to: (a) Increase the capital funds available to minority and womenowned business enterprises based in Washington; and (b) Create jobs and economic opportunities within Washington. (3) Investments under this section must be made in a mannerconsistent with investment or management criteria established by theboard or its executive director. In making investments of money in theWashington growing business fund, the primary investment objective isto maximize the rate of return at a level consistent with the otherfunds under the control of the board, at a prudent level of risk, asrequired by RCW 43.33A.110. (a) In choosing among equal investment opportunities that satisfythis primary investment objective, the board shall give priority tothose investments from the account that assist startup and expandingWashingtonbased businesses. (b) Assets in the fund shall be diversified across differentindustry sectors and regions of the state, such that the assets areprudently invested and that jobs and economic opportunity are equitablydistributed across the entire state and encouraged in those communitieswhich are economically distressed. (4) A management company selected to manage a portion of theWashington growing business fund shall manage the money in the account,subject to the investment policies established by the state investmentboard, with the care, skill, and diligence required by RCW 43.33A.110.In selecting management companies, the board shall consider thepotential company's physical and employment presence in Washington aswell as a demonstrable ability to find investment opportunities incommunities throughout the state. (5) As used in this section: (a) "Emerging business" means: HB 1594 p. 2 (i) A business with its principal place of business located in thisstate or with a substantial employment base in Washington; (ii) A business with average annual gross receipts over the lastthree years not exceeding one million dollars for construction firmsand three hundred thousand dollars for nonconstruction firms; (iii) A business with fewer than twenty employees; (iv) An independent business; and (v) A business properly licensed and legally registered in thisstate. An "emerging business" does not mean a subsidiary or parent companybelonging to a group of firms which are owned and controlled by thesame individuals which have aggregate annual gross receipts in excessof one million dollars for construction firms or three hundred thousanddollars for nonconstruction firms. (b) "Minority and womenowned business enterprise" means anyresident minority business enterprise or women's business enterprise,certified as such by the office of minority and women's businessenterprises under chapter 39.19 RCW. (c) "Startup business" means a Washington business in the act orinstance of being set in operation around a technology, product, orservice based on a sound business plan.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 43.33A RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The board and its designees must include in their statement ofinvestment principles: The extent, if at all, to which social,environmental, or ethical considerations are taken into account intheir selection, retention, and realization of investments; and theirpolicy, if any, in relation to the exercise of rights, including votingrights, attaching to investments.
